title: Histology, Tissue Processing and High Content Microscopy
text: Histology, Tissue Processing and High Content Microscopy Core The Histology, Tissue Processing and High Content Microscopy Core will continue to serve the needs of UCSD vision researchers by providing dedicated tissue processing equipment and a part-time histotechnician experienced in eye histology and immunohistochemistry. The Histology, Tissue Processing and High Content Microscopy Core supports both paraffin and cryosection processing and various staining strategies. The core also provides vision researchers with 1) advice for fixation selection depending on study purpose; 2) paraffin and cryo blocking of study samples; 3) paraffin or cryo histology slide preparation with customized staining, 4) assistance for proper interpretation and precision microsampling of the region of interest for electron microscopy evaluation and 5) high content confocal imaging for drug screening and histologic specimen imaging.

title: Integrative genomic and functional genomic studies to connect variant to function for CAD GWAS loci
text:
Genome-wide association studies have identified over 200 independent loci that influence coronary artery
disease (CAD) risk, yet determining the causal genes connecting genetic variation to disease susceptibility has
lagged. Leveraging computational pipelines and machine learning models using large-scale functional genomic
datasets, and scalable functional genomic screens with targeted validation, our study systematically identifies
the functional regulatory elements that contain the risk variants and regulate the expression of target genes and
phenotypic outcomes at CAD loci. Our results provide (1) novel insights into tissue/cell type-specific contributions
to the genetic basis of CAD, and (2) an innovative computational and experimental framework for systematic
variant-to-function discoveries.

title: Surveillance to track and characterize antimalarial resistance trends in Ugandan Plasmodium falciparum parasites (STARTUP)
text:
Leveraging our extensive infrastructure and ongoing research activities in Uganda, we will characterize
emerging antimalarial resistance at field sites across Uganda. We will use molecular, parasitological and
epidemiological approaches to better understand the extent and origins of drug resistance, the genotypes that
contribute to resistance, and the epidemiological factors that facilitate the evolution of resistant parasites.

title: Molecular Determinants of Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease in Multi-ethnic Populations
text:
Understanding the process of atherosclerosis and its progression is essential to decrease cardiovascular
disease burden. Our goal is to use multi-omics technologies to identify novel genetic determinants and
metabolites associated with atherosclerosis so that more efficacious intervention strategies can be
appropriately administered. The results of this research will enable continued scientific progress toward an
understanding of cardiovascular disease etiology.

title: Molecular recording to understand the determinants of cell fate transitions in early development
text:
The goal of this project is to develop molecular recording methods to record and recover key
determinants in cell-fate transitions during early development. We propose to test and optimize our methods in
synthetic embryo models that mimic the early mammalian development process. We anticipate that these
experiments will deepen the current model of mammalian early development and substantially advance
molecular recording technology.

title: CASCADE: A North Carolina cohort to address the cascading effects of the HIV and substance use syndemic
text: The South continues to bear the greatest burden of HIV in the United States. People who use drugs (PWUD) like stimulants and opioids are less likely to receive evidence-based HIV prevention and treatment services. This cohort study applies an observational-implementation hybrid approach to understanding the multilevel factors that impact substance use and HIV outcomes, with the goal of improving health outcomes for all PWUD.

title: Structure and Function of Pentameric Ligand-gated Ion Channels
text:
The pentameric ligand-gated ion channels (pLGICs) mediate fast synaptic transmission in the central and
peripheral nervous systems and hence, critically govern numerous cellular processes such as pain perception,
motor coordination, and gastrointestinal functions. Dysfunctions in pLGICs are associated with several
psychiatric, neurological, and gastrointestinal disorders. The goal of the proposed studies is to elucidate
fundamental mechanisms governing channel function and modulation at a molecular level, and thereby aid drug
development strategies.

title: Characterizing Oncogenic Nras in IDH1 Mutant AML Leukemogenesis and Therapeutic Responsiveness
text:
Despite advancements in treating isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutated acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with
targeted differentiation therapy, oncogenic Nras mutations consistently predict resistance. This proposal will
characterize the role of oncogenic Nras in IDH mutant AML leukemogenesis and responsiveness to
differentiation therapy with the goal of identifying novel therapeutic targets for this high-risk patient group. Using
clinically relevant mouse models and patient samples, this work will elucidate how signaling environments
influence a cell’s differentiation state and how cell state subsequently influences response to differentiation
therapy.

title: T cell expression of inflammatory chemokine receptors
text:
In chronic autoimmune conditions, lymphocytes migrate into inflamed tissues by following specific sets of homing
signals released from the tissue. This project aims to discovery signals and molecular regulators that control
expression of homing receptors on human T cells, with the goal of modulating these signals to inhibit trafficking
T cell trafficking to inflamed sites in autoimmune diseases.

title: Multimodal approach to decipher CIC::DUX4 sarcoma
text:
The emergence of CIC::DUX4 sarcoma (CDS) as a distinct small round blue cell sarcoma with aggressive
chemo-refractory behavior highlights the urgent need for novel targeted therapies. Despite recent molecular
insights, the rarity of CDS samples and the absence of robust experimental models hinder our understanding of
its biology, posing challenges for diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic development. Through this grant
proposal, we outline a multifaceted strategy employing cutting-edge in vivo modeling to dissect the early
molecular drivers of malignancy, with a particular emphasis on immune evasion mechanisms, while providing
compelling proof-of-concept for precision therapies that selectively disrupt the oncogenic CIC::DUX4/P300/CBP
axis.

title: Refining Small-Area Cancer Surveillance Through AI-Driven Spatial Clustering
text:
This project will use advanced Geographic Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) methods to create sub-county
geographic zones aimed to improve how cancer registry data is aggregated and reported in Texas. By
addressing the limitations of county-based reporting, especially in sparsely populated rural and
demographically complex urban areas, we aim to reduce data suppression and identify previously hidden
geographic patterns of cancer burden. The resulting zones will enable more targeted prevention and control
efforts for breast, colorectal, and lung cancers.

title: AI SWG
text: Artificial intelligence and advanced data science methods offer powerful tools for analyzing complex biomedical and population-level datasets relevant to HIV prevention, treatment, and cure research. The AI SWG strengthens the capacity of investigators to apply these approaches to HIV research, ultimately supporting innovative strategies to improve HIV prevention and treatment outcomes.

title: Overcoming Therapy Resistance in Fusion Oncoprotein Driven Pediatric Leukemia
text:
NUP98-NSD1 fusion-positive acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a poor prognostic subtype in children and
is frequently associated with co-occurring mutations in the transcription factor WT1. Focusing on the cellular and
developmental context, our proposal aims to dissect mechanisms of action of the fusion oncoprotein NUP98-
NSD1, investigate WT1's role in therapy resistance, and identify novel therapeutic targets for childhood AML.
These results are poised to reshape our understanding of childhood susceptibility to AML and provide a rationale
for therapeutic intervention in future clinical studies.

title: Project 2: Developing Novel Combination Immunotherapeutics for Non–Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer
text:
Non–muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) is the most common presentation of bladder cancer and is
characterized by frequent recurrence and resistance to standard therapies, resulting in significant morbidity,
mortality, and healthcare cost, underscoring the urgent need for novel treatment strategies. Fc-engineered
antibodies agonizing CD40 (e.g., 2141-V11) have shown superior antitumor activity and promising clinical
responses in bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG)-unresponsive NMIBC, yet the mechanisms driving this efficacy
remain unclear. Our goal is to elucidate how dendritic cells mediate immune response to CD40 agonism, BCG,
and other immunotherapies to inform rational design of future combination strategies for patients with NMIBC.

title: Moving beyond the Pain-Suicidality Link: An Investigation of Fluctuations in Social Threat and Neural Response to Social Threat in Momentary Pain and Proximal Risk for Suicidal Ideation in Adolescence
text:
Findings will advance understanding beyond the pain–suicidality link by pinpointing (a) proximal factors
predicting when suicidal ideation (SI) occurs (i.e., in moments of social threat or physical pain), (b) neural
vulnerability markers identifying who develops SI, and (c) how SI may develop through interactions between
negative social environments and altered function in the pain system. Findings will inform novel targets for just-
in-time interventions that deliver skills through electronic devices in critical moments of risk. Additionally,
findings may help refine or augment other existing interventions for SI among vulnerable youth by integrating
treatment components that target physical pain in the context of social threat, such as cognitive-behavioral
therapies established for pain, or non-invasive fMRI real-time neurofeedback in which youth learn to regulate
brain activation in key pain-related brain regions.

title: A cross-species preclinical platform to enhance the translation of new medicines
text:
Gene therapies for the disease of contractile muscle are extraordinarily difficult to develop and have a track
record of significant adverse effects during clinical trials, including patient death. We will develop an in vitro
model of contractility using both human and murine cells that can be used to pre-clinically test these therapies
in a way that can translate results from animal to human studies. We will also use the platform to assess the
viability of a revolutionary novel genetic medicine for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

title: Investigating the Role of Cell Adhesion Molecule 1 and Focal Adhesion Kinase in Mast Cell-Sensory Neuron Interactions to Drive IgE Mediated Anaphylaxis
text:
Anaphylaxis is a potentially fatal allergic reaction that occurs within minutes of exposure to an allergen, with no
available therapies that can block the reaction from occurring. In in vitro experiments, cell adhesion molecule-1
(CADM1) is necessary for the binding of mast cells (MC) to sensory neurons, and focal adhesion kinase (FAK)
is needed for MC activation. This project aims to define a role for FAK and CADM1 in mast cell-sensory neuron
interactions during allergen induced anaphylaxis, which will provide insight into the propagation of anaphylaxis
and potential therapeutic targets.

title: Targeted Degradation of Mycobacterial PknG for Host Control of Tuberculosis
text:
Tuberculosis (TB) is the single leading cause of death from infectious disease and new drugs are urgently
needed to kill the causative agent, Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), within its predominant host cell niche, the
macrophage. Mtb’s ability to replicate within the macrophage and break out to infect other cells depends on an
Mtb enzyme called protein kinase G (PknG) that enters the macrophage cytosol. Here we will synthesize
compounds to direct macrophage’s protein degradation machinery to degrade the invading Mtb’s PknG, thereby
advancing the emerging concept of targeted protein degradation for anti-microbial development.

title: DOT1L-Mediated H3K79 Methylation as a Regulator of Histone Variant H3.3 and Neuronal Development
text:
Neurodevelopmental disorders are commonly caused by genetic variants in chromatin regulators. Disruption of
histone 3 lysine 79 (H3K79) methylation is implicated in a recently identified neurodevelopmental disorder
caused by variants in its methyltransferase DOT1L, yet how this modification regulates chromatin to contribute
to brain development remains poorly understood. This project will define the mechanisms by which H3K79me
regulates chromatin and its role in neuronal development and function, providing insight into the molecular basis
of DOT1L-associated neurodevelopmental disorders and advancing our broader understanding of epigenetic
mechanisms underlying neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Advancing MALDI-TOF-Based Microbial and Metabolite Identification Through Machine Learning and Multi-Omics Approaches
text:
This project will develop machine learning-based bioinformatic tools to enable rapid and low-cost identification
of bacteria and their specialized metabolites using MALDI mass spectrometry. These advancements will
improve our ability to characterize microbial communities, accelerating the discovery of health-promoting
compounds and therapies derived from the microbiome. The successful completion of these aims will
enhance our understanding of host–microbiome interactions and support the development of novel strategies
to prevent and treat microbiome-associated diseases
